as_told.title: Eric Hecker: South Pole neutrino emitter and the Christchurch earthquake
as_told.place_text: South Pole, Antarctica; Christchurch, New Zealand

plain: A man named Eric Hecker is said to have worked for the defence company Raytheon in 2011, helping put in a neutrino system a mile under the ice at the South Pole. Neutrinos are tiny particles that pass through almost anything. The UFO researcher Steven Greer repeats this, saying Hecker "came forward" a couple of years ago about a "nutrino light system" buried in the ice. Jay Anderson, another guest, adds that Hecker said he noticed energy "being transferred from one area to another area where it wasn't supposed to be going." Michels himself calls it "a neutrino emitter and detector" and links it to the earthquake in Christchurch, New Zealand, which would mean the system could send out energy as well as just measure it.
